segments.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Der from Gulf Coast Ultrasound Institute. Today I'm going to give you a hot scan tip
about how to stay centered on your target when performing vascular access. So when you're first
learning ultrasound, learners can struggle with keeping their target centered on their ultrasound
machine, particularly when it comes to vascular access. For example, when you're scanning,
in this case on this phantom, you may be rotating from a short axis fever or blood vessel
to long axis view, only to find that as you're turning you slip off your target and then have difficulty
going back to locate the target again. So try this hot tip. Use the M mode on your ultrasound
machine. There should be an M button, you just tap M and that will default to the center of your
ultrasound image. Then line up your target on that M mode line. So in this case I'm going to take
the target blood vessel on my phantom, I'm going to line it up on the M mode line. As I rotate the
transducer, I need to make sure that my target, this blood vessel, stays on the green line.
If I start the rotate the transducer only to find that my target is off, I need to go back
and re-center the target onto the line before I continue the rotation.
So I gently turn my transducer, I'll stabilize with my left hand, I'm staying on the green
line, and then as soon as I complete the rotation, I'm now back on my target.
So by staying on the green line, as you begin to rotate, it'll make sure that you end up on that target location.
So let's try that one more time.
So we slide the target onto the green line, begin the rotation.
And if you start to lose that target off that green line, you'll stop, re-center, and then complete the rotation.
So by using that green M-mode line and slowly turning, keep it on that green line, you'll land on your target every time.
That's my hot tip and now it's your turn to scan.
